name: Short-Stay Visa / Visa-Free Entry

requirements.blocker_text: Citizens of ECOWAS/CEDEAO member states (Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, Ghana, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Togo) enter visa-free, a policy dating to 1980. UAE nationals may obtain a visa on arrival with an ordinary passport; other pre-approved travelers with National Police clearance may get a 'flyer visa' on arrival at Niamey. Everyone else needs a visa arranged in advance. Transit without a visa is allowed up to 24 hours with onward tickets, except for nationals of a short list of countries (including China, Russia, Vietnam) who must stay on the same aircraft. Separately, Ordinance No. 2025-02 (13 January 2025) tightened the GENERAL entry/stay regime for all foreigners regardless of visa status -- valid travel documents are mandatory at entry, a residence permit or resident card becomes mandatory after 3 months for anyone staying (Article 5), and anyone hosting a foreigner (paid or not) must notify local police or face penalties. Violations of the entry/stay rules carry criminal penalties of 2-5 years imprisonment and fines of 5-50 million CFA francs, alongside administrative expulsion, detention, or repatriation.
requirements.fix_path: Non-exempt nationalities must arrange a visa before travel; ECOWAS nationals and a short list of others enter visa-free or with a visa on arrival.

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days before a residence permit/resident card becomes mandatory

STATUS: DRAFT -- the general visa-free/visa-on-arrival list is sourced to Wikipedia, tier 4; the current 2025 ordinance is corroborated by a UNHCR-hosted platform (tier 2) for its core structural articles and by African press (tier 4) for the enforcement/penalty specifics -- no .gov.ne or migration-spccm.ne government source could be fetched (the latter's TLS certificate has expired, the same recurring failure mode seen elsewhere in this dataset, e.g. Mali's diplomatie.gouv.ml). MAJOR CURRENT-EVENT FINDING, flagged prominently as this dataset does for other recent legal reforms: Niger's military government (led by General Tiani since the 2023 coup) enacted Ordinance No. 2025-02 in January 2025, substantially tightening the entry/residence regime with criminal penalties far harsher than most other countries in this dataset (2-5 years imprisonment, 5-50 million CFA fines) -- explicitly framed by the government as a response to 'diplomatic tensions.' CROSS-REFERENCE: Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso jointly left ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, forming the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) -- but as of a 2026 status check, ECOWAS nationals still enter all three countries visa-free 'jusqu'a nouvel ordre' (until further notice); an intervening industry-advisory source predicted this exemption would lapse after a six-month grace period ending July 2025, but that lapse is NOT confirmed to have occurred as of this build -- the 'until further notice' arrangement appears to still be the operative status.
